objective: Run the frozen five-pair Codex-to-Claude Code comparison between compiled-prompt and TORC continuity using enforced, evidence-bearing harness controls.
success_evidence: Every live invocation enforces and records the frozen harness version, model, effort, service tier when applicable, assignment, and tool policy.
Five paired A/C blocks complete in the preregistered order with unique run identifiers.
All included runs verify with accepted dispositions, valid artifact manifests, and clean best-effort credential scans.
The final report includes every registered measure, paired differences, lane medians and ranges, failures, and operator interventions.
non_goals: Changing the P1a fixture, schemas, scorer, normalization, or acceptance thresholds.
Adding another harness, model-based judging, provider SDK integration, or native-persistence substitute.
Claiming statistical significance from five pairs or authorizing P2.
Adding a daemon, service, watcher, network dependency, or parent Lugos edit.
accepted_threats: Live model output and provider latency remain nondeterministic under fixed controls.
The model identifiers are versioned product identifiers but may not expose dated provider snapshots.
Credential-pattern scanning is best-effort and cannot prove arbitrary text contains no secret.
Five pairs support only a bounded comparative conclusion.
